A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Lutetium (루테튬) itself — the sovereign of the Lutetium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: about twenty — a fresh young-adult face; no facial lines.
Face — her own: an elegant, refined presence; porcelain-pale skin; softly tapered face narrowing to a small, soft chin; medium-sized eyes — long phoenix eyes with lifted outer corners, outer eye corners slightly lifted; gracefully arched brows; slim, delicate nose with a refined bridge; soft, full lips; clear crystal-grey eyes with tiny blue flashes; sharp winged eyeliner.
Body and hair: tall and statuesque with long legs and a full, curvaceous figure — full bust and hips, narrow waist build; an asymmetric bob, longer on one side with asymmetric bangs; silver-white hair with a cool slate sheen and tiny blue flashes like a scintillating crystal.
Expression: a composed, self-assured look.
Her element, carried in her design: lutetium: a hard, dense silvery-white metal, the last and smallest of the fifteen lanthanides and the hardest and densest of them; found in 1907 by a Paris chemist, also a painter and sculptor, who split the earth called ytterbia once more and named the hidden younger element for Lutetia, the old Latin name of Paris, while a rival in Austria called it cassiopeium; woven with silicon and oxygen into scintillator crystals it throws a tiny flash of blue light each time a gamma ray strikes, the eyes of PET scanners; its slow decay over some thirty-seven billion years dates meteorites and the oldest rocks.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — MECHA
Costume: she is a female mecha personification — plates, joints, binders and glow lines carry the traits above; the plates must read as solid armor with visible joints, not as cloth or a gown; a back unit may carry the motif. A long coat of rigid hard silver-white plates from the shoulders to below the knees, open at the front over slate-grey body armor, an angular high black collar, rows of small clear crystal blocks set along the coat edges that flash blue one after another, a ring-shaped crystal emblem at the chest; the plates must read as solid armor, not a gown.
Silhouette: a long coat made of rigid plates from the shoulders to below the knees, open at the front to show the body armor, with an angular collar. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette.
Colours: hard silver-white, scintillation blue flash, river slate grey, Parisian cream and soft black.
Exposure (bold): her mecha frame is cut open by design in only these places — bare shoulders and upper arms between pauldron and gauntlet, and a deep open chest window with natural cleavage framed by the chest plates; everywhere else she stays fully plated. The plates stay on, fitted and symmetrical, with skin clearly showing in each opening. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; keep the plate material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: year 2200, a city that sees inside: great rings of scintillator crystal arching over a gallery, flashing blue as they draw the hidden inside of everything that passes through, an archive vault where meteorites and ancient rock cores are dated by a thirty-seven-billion-year clock, slender white towers rebuilt on an island in a wide river.
This card: under great rings of crystal flashing blue as things pass through.
Pose: Standing turned three-quarters toward the camera, weight on one leg, one hand resting at her side or hip.
Light: the scene's own light, rendered the way this style renders light and skin.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Lu) and atomic number (71) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish.
